issues.t: Coolant leak from water pump or thermostat housing
issues.sym: A low coolant warning, a sweet smell after driving, pink crust near the engine, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: The 2.0L turbo engine uses a plastic water pump and thermostat housing that can warp and seep. Audi has issued repeated service bulletins for coolant leaks on both Q3 generations.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure tested. Top up only with Audi-approved coolant and stop driving if the engine overheats.

issues.t: Water leaks in through the roof and map lights
issues.sym: Water dripping from the overhead map lights or headliner after rain or a car wash, damp carpets, or a musty smell.
issues.why: The sunroof drain tubes clog with debris or come loose, so water that should drain out runs into the headliner instead.
issues.next: Have the sunroof drains cleared and checked. Dry the interior quickly to avoid mold and damage to wiring.

issues.t: Carbon buildup on intake valves
issues.sym: Rough idle, hesitation, misfire codes and a flashing or steady check engine light.
issues.why: The direct-injection 2.0L turbo sprays fuel straight into the cylinders, so carbon from oil vapor builds up on the intake valves over time. RepairPal lists this as the most-reported Q3 problem.
issues.next: If misfires keep coming back after new coils and plugs, have a shop inspect the intake valves. Walnut blasting is the usual cleaning.

issues.t: Timing chain stretch with camshaft timing codes
issues.sym: A rattle after a cold start and a check engine light with a crankshaft-camshaft correlation code (P0016). Severe cases run rough or will not start.
issues.why: The timing chain or its tensioner wears, letting cam timing drift. Audi issued bulletins on the P0016 code, and owners report chain failures at high mileage.
issues.next: Have a shop measure chain stretch if you get timing codes or hear a cold-start rattle. Regular oil changes with the right oil help the chain last.

issues.t: Engine uses too much oil
issues.sym: The low oil warning comes on between services and you need to add oil regularly.
issues.why: Audi 2.0T engines of this period, including the Q3, were part of complaints and a lawsuit over piston rings that let oil burn.
issues.next: Check the oil at every fill-up and ask the dealer for an oil consumption test. Rule out a failed PCV valve or leaks first.

issues.t: Turbocharger failure
issues.sym: Loss of power, a whine or whistle from the engine, blue or gray smoke, and boost-related warning codes.
issues.why: Owners report turbochargers failing around 55,000 miles, usually from worn bearings or a failing wastegate.
issues.next: Stop hard driving and have the turbo inspected. Check oil level often; a turbo running low on oil fails quickly.

issues.t: Cracked cylinder head
issues.sym: Coolant loss with no visible leak, white exhaust smoke, overheating or misfires.
issues.why: Some high-mileage 2015 Q3 owners report cracked cylinder heads, often after overheating.
issues.next: If coolant keeps disappearing, have a pressure and combustion-leak test done before driving further.

issues.t: Windshield cracks with no impact
issues.sym: A crack appears in the windshield without a rock strike, sometimes very early in the car's life.
issues.why: Owners report windshields cracking on their own, likely from stress at the glass edges.
issues.next: Have it replaced if the crack is in your line of sight. Ask the dealer if it is covered under warranty.

issues.t: Oil leak from the quattro transfer box
issues.sym: Gear oil drips under the front center of the car, sometimes with a burning smell from the exhaust area.
issues.why: Audi issued bulletins for oil leaks at the bevel box (the transfer unit that sends power to the rear wheels on quattro models).
issues.next: Have the leak found and fixed. Running the bevel box low on oil can destroy it.

issues.t: A/C stops cooling from a refrigerant leak
issues.sym: The air conditioning blows warm or only slightly cool air.
issues.why: Audi issued bulletins for A/C systems losing their refrigerant, including leaking refrigerant hoses and repairs needing a new compressor.
issues.next: Have the A/C leak tested with dye or a sniffer before recharging. Recharging alone will not last if there is a leak.

issues.t: Battery drains and the car will not start
issues.sym: The car is dead or cranks slowly after sitting for a day or more.
issues.why: Audi issued bulletins for low battery voltage causing no-starts, including a stability control module that kept drawing power after parking.
issues.next: Have the battery tested and a parasitic draw test done. Ask the dealer about software updates.

issues.t: Clunk from the rear suspension over bumps
issues.sym: A rattle or clunk from the back of the car over potholes and rough roads.
issues.why: Audi issued a bulletin for rattling or clunking from the rear suspension, usually from worn bushings or loose parts.
issues.next: Have the rear suspension inspected for worn bushings, links and shock mounts.

issues.t: Cracking noise from the front when steering
issues.sym: A cracking or spring-jumping noise from the front when turning the wheel or maneuvering slowly.
issues.why: Audi issued bulletins for a cracking noise from the front strut mounts and springs on these cars.
issues.next: Have the front strut mounts checked. The fix is usually a revised part under warranty.

issues.t: Check engine light with camshaft timing or misfire codes
issues.sym: Check engine light with codes like P0011, and possibly a rough idle.
issues.why: Audi issued several bulletins for this code on the newer 2.0L engine, often related to camshaft timing control.
issues.next: Have the dealer read the codes and check for updates or bulletin repairs.

issues.t: Steering rack mounting bolt can corrode and break (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or looseness in the steering. If the bolt breaks, steering control can be affected.
issues.why: The right-side steering rack mounting bolt can corrode and snap.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have the free repair done.

issues.t: Brake pedal plate can bend or come off (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal may feel wrong under hard braking, or in a worst case detach.
issues.why: A poor weld on the brake pedal plate can let it bend or separate during hard stops.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the pedal inspected and replaced for free if needed.

issues.t: Passenger air bag may not deploy properly (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. In a crash, the passenger air bag may not come through the dashboard correctly.
issues.why: The tear seam in the dashboard above the passenger air bag may not open as designed.
issues.next: Check your VIN and book the free inspection.

issues.t: Tire pressure warning may come on too late (recall)
issues.sym: No everyday symptom. If all four tires lose pressure together, the warning may come late.
issues.why: A software issue in the tire pressure monitor.
issues.next: Check tire pressures monthly and get the free software update.

issues.t: Rear seat belts may not hold a child seat (recall)
issues.sym: The rear belt's child-seat locking mode may release, so a child seat installed with the belt may loosen.
issues.why: The automatic locking retractor in some rear belts can switch off too early.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Use the LATCH anchors for child seats until the belts are checked.

issues.t: Fuel can spill from the filler neck (recall)
issues.sym: Fuel smell or fuel spilling out of the filler area when refueling.
issues.why: The fuel tank vent pipe could be damaged during assembly.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the tank and canister inspected for free.

issues.t: Rear window can crack or break (recall)
issues.sym: The rear window cracks or shatters without an obvious impact.
issues.why: A manufacturing error in some rear windows.
issues.next: Check your VIN; the dealer checks the glass date code and replaces it if needed.

issues.t: Backup camera image does not show (recall)
issues.sym: No camera picture, or a blank screen, when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: Software errors and, on some cars, infotainment unit damage at shutoff can stop the rear camera image.
issues.next: Check your VIN; there are several related recalls. Look behind you carefully until fixed.

issues.t: Passenger seat sensor connection can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger air bag off light may come on with an adult in the seat.
issues.why: The connector to the passenger occupant detection module can loosen and switch off the front passenger air bag.
issues.next: Check your VIN and book the free module replacement.

issues.t: Rear camera can fail to show an image at start-up (recall)
issues.sym: The rearview camera picture does not appear when reversing.
issues.why: A start-up error in the camera control unit.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the free software update done.

issues.t: Failed turn signal may not be flagged on the dash (recall)
issues.sym: A front turn signal bulb can be out without the dashboard warning you.
issues.why: A body control module software issue.
issues.next: Walk around the car to check signals and have the free software update done.

issues.t: Brake lights may stay off during emergency braking (recall)
issues.sym: If you use the parking brake switch to stop in an emergency, the brake lights may not come on.
issues.why: A software issue in the emergency braking function.
issues.next: Check your VIN and get the free software update.

issues.t: Side marker lights can switch off (recall)
issues.sym: The side marker lights are off while the parking lights or headlights are on.
issues.why: A lighting software error.
issues.next: Check your VIN and get the free software update.

issues.t: Sunroof can keep closing after shut-off (recall)
issues.sym: The sunroof continues to close after the car is turned off, with a pinch risk.
issues.why: Sunroof control software on cars built April to November 2014.
issues.next: Check your VIN and get the free software update.
